# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # We install to /usr/local, a standard location for system-wide libraries.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Replaced the 'make config'-based build with a standard, more robust CMake build process.
    # This directly invokes cmake for configuration, build, and installation steps.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && cmake . -B build -DSHARED=1 -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && cmake --build build -j$(nproc) \
    && cmake --install build \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Explicitly set the source directory with '-S .' to prevent CMake path ambiguity errors.
    # This is the modern, recommended syntax for out-of-source builds.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && cmake -S . -B build -DSHARED=1 -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && cmake --build build -j$(nproc) \
    && cmake --install build \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Switched from a direct cmake call to using the provided 'make config' wrapper,
    # which correctly sets up the build environment and avoids path resolution issues.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Cloned the specific tag directly to avoid checkout errors with shallow clones.
    && git clone --branch v5.1.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    # FIX: Corrected MFEM_USE_MPI variable to lowercase 'yes' as expected by the makefile.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Removed `--depth 1` to perform a full clone, ensuring the specified tag can be cloned reliably.
    && git clone --branch v5.1.0 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir-p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Switched to a standard clone followed by a checkout of the 'v5.1.0' tag,
    # as the '--branch' flag cannot be used for tags.
    && git clone https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && git checkout v5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    # FIX: Corrected typo in mkdir command (was mkdir-p).
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # A specific tag is checked out for version stability.
    && git clone https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && git checkout v5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Switched to a more robust full clone followed by an explicit checkout of the tag.
    && git clone https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git \
    && cd METIS \
    && git checkout v5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # FIX: Download the source tarball directly to avoid git clone issues with tags.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone and build the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # The 'make parallel' target builds MFEM with MPI enabled.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make install prefix=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Download the source tarball directly to avoid git clone issues with tags.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    # FIX: Combined 'parallel' and 'install' targets to ensure MFEM_USE_MPI=yes
    # is applied to both, so the parallel library is correctly installed.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable without specifying its full path.
    && install -s laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source control, certificates for secure connections,
    # and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Switched to the more robust CMake build system for METIS to prevent script execution errors.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the METIS installation in /usr/local.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # FIX: The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', so we must install that file.
    # The destination is 'laghos' to match the CMD instruction.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    # FIX: Add libhypre-dev, a required dependency for the parallel MFEM build.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Switched to the more robust CMake build system for METIS to prevent script execution errors.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # FIX: Use 'make parallel' to build and 'make p-install' to install the parallel library.
    # The 'install' target installs the serial version, which is incorrect for this build.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    && make p-install MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', so we must install that file.
    # The destination is 'laghos' to match the CMD instruction.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Switched to the more robust CMake build system for METIS to prevent script execution errors.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # FIX: Disable SIMD auto-detection to prevent exec format errors in cross-platform builds.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO \
    && make p-install MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', so we must install that file.
    # The destination is 'laghos' to match the CMD instruction.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Switched to the more robust CMake build system for METIS to prevent script execution errors.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # FIX: Use a single 'p-install' command. It builds and installs, ensuring all flags
    # (like MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO) are applied consistently to prevent build errors.
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', so we must install that file.
    # The destination is 'laghos' to match the CMD instruction.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install the METIS graph partitioning library, a dependency for MFEM.
    # Switched to the more robust CMake build system for METIS to prevent script execution errors.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # FIX: Pinned to stable release v4.6 to ensure compatibility and a reliable build.
    && git clone --branch v4.6 --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    # FIX: Pinned to stable release v4.0, which is compatible with recent MFEM versions.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone --branch v4.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', so we must install that file.
    # The destination is 'laghos' to match the CMD instruction.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install METIS v5.1.0, a dependency for MFEM.
    # We download a stable release tarball and use CMake for a robust build.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # A stable release (v4.6) is used for a reproducible, production-ready build.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    && git clone --branch v4.6 --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    # A stable release (v4.0) is used for compatibility with the chosen MFEM version.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone --branch v4.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', which is installed as 'laghos'
    # to match the CMD instruction and for ease of use.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install METIS v5.1.0, a dependency for MFEM.
    # A stable release tarball and CMake are used for a robust build of this dependency.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # SIMD is disabled for robust cross-platform builds (e.g., using QEMU).
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', which is installed as 'laghos'
    # to match the CMD instruction and for ease of use.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install METIS v5.1.0, a dependency for MFEM.
    # A stable release tarball and CMake are used for a robust build of this dependency.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # SIMD is disabled for robust cross-platform builds (e.g., using QEMU).
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', which is installed as 'laghos'
    # to match the CMD instruction and for ease of use.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, recent LTS release.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Avoids interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication defaults to TCP over the primary
# network interface (eth0), which is standard in Docker/Kubernetes.
# It explicitly disables InfiniBand (openib) and shared-memory (vader) BTLs,
# which are not typically available or can cause issues in this environment.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib,vader
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=ssh

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build the application.
# This adheres to the strict 'no multi-stage' and 'no COPY/ADD' constraints.
# The image will contain all build tools, but the build cache is cleaned up.
RUN \
    # 1. Install system dependencies
    # Includes build tools, compilers, Git, certificates, OpenMPI, and Hypre.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # 2. Create directories for building and for the final application source
    && mkdir -p /build /app \
    && cd /build \
    # 3. Build and install METIS v5.1.0, a dependency for MFEM.
    # A stable release tarball and CMake are used for a robust build of this dependency.
    && wget -q -O metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf metis-v5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-v5.1.0 \
    && cmake . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSHARED=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd /build \
    # 4. Clone, build, and install the parallel version of the MFEM finite element library.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    # It will automatically detect the system-installed METIS and Hypre libraries.
    # SIMD is disabled for robust cross-platform builds (e.g., using QEMU).
    && git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make p-install -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=yes MFEM_USE_SIMD=NO MFEM_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 5. Update the dynamic linker cache to find the newly installed shared libraries.
    && ldconfig \
    # 6. Clone the Laghos application source code into its final location.
    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', which is installed as 'laghos'
    # to match the CMD instruction and for ease of use.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]

    # Clones the latest development branch as requested.
    && cd /app \
    && git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git laghos \
    && cd laghos \
    # 7. Build the parallel version of Laghos ('make p').
    # We point it to the MFEM installation directory.
    && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    # 8. Install the 'laghos' executable to a location on the system's PATH.
    # The parallel build creates 'laghos-p', which is installed as 'laghos'
    # to match the CMD instruction and for ease of use.
    && install -s laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos \
    # 9. Clean up the build directory to reduce the final image size.
    && rm -rf /build

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source directory.
# This ensures that the './data' directory required by the application is present at runtime,
# satisfying the constraint to make data files available without using COPY or ADD.
WORKDIR /app/laghos

# Set the default command for the container.
# This will execute the Laghos application when the container is run without any other arguments.
CMD ["laghos"]
